description: I'm a maker interested in electronics, software, and accessible design. With ORBIT — Earth in Tune, I aim to explore Earth imagery through sound and descriptions, especially for people who are blind or have low vision. My focus is hardware–software integration and prototyping. I'm participating solo and not recruiting, but welcome ideas and feedback from people with skills in accessibility, sound design, Earth science, and UX.
summary: P.T.S. (Pixel That Sounds) is a web listening guide that turns NASA Earth imagery into sound, so that people who are blind or have low vision can explore it too. On a turning globe the user picks one of three regions (Amazon, Congo, Antarctica) and hears what the colours of a NASA visualization mean: lightning maps become rain and thunder, sea-surface temperature colours become a singing voice, and aerosol smoke becomes coughs. Each sound is rendered from the pixels of the image by documented, repeatable rules: stronger pixels produce a more intense sound. The whole site works by keyboard, screen reader and voice control in English and Italian. It addresses the challenge by making NASA Earth data accessible beyond sight, because data that can only be seen excludes millions of people.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

P.T.S. opens on a slowly turning Earth with three pins. Choosing a place opens a player with the NASA image, its legend, its source and a 15-second sound made from that image. A guided tour plays the six sounds in sequence, and a content list reaches all nine views without using the globe.

HOW IT WORKS

1. We selected NASA visualizations and grouped them into three categories: lightning flash rate, sea-surface temperature colours, and aerosols.

2. Each category has one recorded base sound: rain and thunder, a singing voice, coughs.

3. The image is scanned left to right and the intensity of its pixels shapes the sound. A brighter lightning map gives heavier rain and more thunder; more smoke gives more coughs; colder ocean colours give a deeper voice.

The rules are published with the code, and every track can be rebuilt and checked against its checksum.

ACCESSIBILITY

- Voice control in English and Italian: every button has a spoken command, from entering the site to pausing a sound.

- Keyboard and screen-reader support with named native controls, visible focus and announced state changes; a braille display works through the screen reader.

- A spoken description, legend and source for every image, on request.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Earth observation is communicated almost entirely through colour maps. P.T.S. shows that the same information can be offered through hearing, with a method that is transparent and can be extended to other NASA datasets and regions. It is meant for blind and low-vision people, and for classrooms and museums that want another way into Earth data.

TOOLS

Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript modules with no framework and no build step; WebGL for the globe; the Web Audio and Web Speech APIs for playback level, speech and voice control; Python (NumPy, SciPy) and Node.js with ffmpeg for the image-to-sound renderer; GitHub Pages for hosting. AI assistance was used for code, audio rendering, the film and documentation, and the film's narration uses ElevenLabs voices.

CREATIVITY

Instead of abstract tones, we chose sounds people already understand: rain for lightning, a human voice for the ocean, coughing for polluted air. The Amazon and the Congo can be compared by ear: rain alone against heavier rain with thunder.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

We state limits openly. The sounds are designed metaphors of image colours, not measurements of rainfall, storm severity or air quality. The Antarctic lightning image has no usable overlay, so its wind is announced as illustrative. The source images cover different periods and no change over time is claimed. Tests with screen-reader users and listeners are still to be done.

LINKS

Live demo: https://pixelthatsounds.github.io/

29-second film: https://pixelthatsounds.github.io/film/pts-promo-29s.mp4

Code: https://github.com/pixelthatsounds/pixelthatsounds.github.io
